Nina (AE): quick sync re: NexaHealth presale. Execs want commit recommendation today. Need throughput sizing, reserved GPU ask, autoscale policy, and HIPAA/security blockers.
Ravi-SE: what does their traffic look like? mix of summarization, chat, and nightly embedding rebuilds?
Nina (AE): yes. Primary is clinical note summarization (avg input ~3000 tokens), chat triage ~80 rps steady, embeddings batch jobs overnight (1M docs, run nightly). They expect short promo spikes ~1.2k rps for ~5m during user events.
Lena-Eng: large context changes things. For 3k tokens summaries latency cost skyrockets. My rough baseline: 6 reserved GPUs (A100-80 equiv) to cover steady summarization + chat if using a quantized 13B variant; plus a burst pool of up to 12 GPUs for promos and nightly embedding parallelism.
Ravi-SE: can we be more precise?
Lena-Eng: sketch: steady load requires ~5.5k token-rate/sec equivalent. If 13B-q4 uses 0.7 tokens/ms on A100-80, we need 6 GPUs reserved. Nightly embeddings we schedule into off-peak and leverage spot/burst credits.
Ravi-SE: autoscale config proposal:```
min_reserved: 6
burst_max: 12
embed_pool_schedule: 02:00-05:00 UTC
scale_up_policy: avg_gpu_latency > 200ms for 20s OR queue_length > 50
scale_down_policy: avg_gpu_latency < 80ms for 90s
prewarm_mode: cold_attach_disabled; use instant-attach prewarmed nodes
kv_prefix_cache: enabled; preheat_window: 15m before event
```
Nina (AE): preheat sounds key. How do we run warmup without touching PHI?
Priya-Security: for HIPAA we must avoid sending real PHI to hosted warmup endpoints. Options: 1) synthetic but realistic prompt sets (recommended), 2) run warmup inside their VPC private deployment. We'll need BAAs, KMS CMEK, and audit logs.
Lena-Eng: also recommend using a smaller-quality model variant as graceful fallback during extreme overload to keep throughput (e.g., 13B -> 7B quantized). We'll route non-critical summary requests to degraded model.
Nina (AE): pricing ask: they want a fixed blended rate for reserved + burst and a line-item for nightly embedding runs. Any quick rule of thumb?
Ravi-SE: ballpark: reserved commit gives ~35-45% off on-demand GPU-hours depending on term; burst billed at on-demand. Embedding jobs billed as batch compute hours (discounts available if scheduled and committed). I'll get CFO numbers.
Priya-Security: checklist for deal room: BAA signed, SOC2 report, encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS, HSM for key custody if requested, VPC peering options, and documented data flow diagrams.
Provision Bot: job queued: preheat-warmup/nexa-1746654321. Start 1746654400.
Lena-Eng: warmup plan: run synthetic 2000 prompts with redacted placeholders, 50 parallel workers over 10m, validate: p95 token latency < 500ms for 3k-contexts, no GPU OOMs, and embedding job completes at target throughput.
Ravi-SE: add checkpoint: run smaller scale test that reproduces long-context memory pressure (KV cache stress) before full heat.
Nina (AE): action items: @Lena-Eng run smoke warmup + KV stress test (owner), @Ravi-SE produce pricing ballpark and commit options (owner), @Priya-Security assemble HIPAA docs & BAA template (owner). I'll ask Nexa infra for VPC contact and confirm acceptable synthetic prompt policy.
Priya-Security: note: if they require on-prem air-gapped deployment we need 8-10% extra GPU capacity for admin and backups; flag to legal on licensing.
Lena-Eng: one more ops note: enforce burst_pool_max with a circuit-breaker that drops to degraded model if queue > 200 for > 60s.
Nina (AE): perfect. I'll update Nexa with the plan and ask for golden prompts and preferred blackout windows for nightly embeddings.
Provision Bot: warmup started 1746654400. Results posted to deal room when done.
Ravi-SE: thanks team. We'll iterate after the smoke results. End.
